page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance driven by the AWS Nitro System and powered by an arm64-based AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 8 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution, paired with 64 GB of memory to establish an 8:1 RAM-to-core ratio. Local ephemeral storage is bundled via a 474 GB NVMe SSD volume. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps, and no discrete graphics processing units are present.

Benchmark profiles indicate steady multi-core execution offset by lower single-threaded throughput. Multi-core performance reaches mid-tier benchmark levels, registered at 12,133.23 in stress-ng and 5,344.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, with dependable performance in clang compilation and database operations. Conversely, single-core processing demonstrates lower relative throughput, with Geekbench single-core and compression tests placing in the lower percentiles. The memory subsystem maintains balanced bandwidth, achieving 101.11 GB/sec in uncached read tests and sustaining 9.53 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks.

The combination of high memory density and high-speed local NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for applications that would otherwise be bounded by network storage latency. While the architecture is less suited for single-threaded batch compression or compute-heavy linear algebra, the r6gd.2xlarge is structured for memory-intensive workloads including Redis and Memcached caching tiers, relational database engines, search indexing, and real-time data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro architecture and powered by an arm64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor at 2.5 GHz. The instance supplies 8 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution, 64 GB of memory, and a direct-attached 474 GB NVMe SSD volume, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates balanced multi-core execution and reliable memory bandwidth, reaching 9.53 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Conversely, single-threaded performance and compression speeds reside in lower percentiles. The presence of high memory capacity alongside fast local NVMe storage provides strong architectural efficiency for data-intensive workloads, making the instance an effective platform for in-memory caches, relational database systems, search clusters, and real-time analytical processing environments.
